question: What term describes the collection of microbes normally living on body surfaces?
explanation: Microbes that routinely inhabit body surfaces without causing disease in healthy individuals are called normal flora. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which body site is normally colonized by indigenous microbiota?
explanation: Surfaces exposed to the outside environment, such as the skin and gut, harbor normal flora. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h1)

question: Microbes that temporarily inhabit the skin for a short period are called what?
explanation: Transient microbes are picked up from the environment and remain on the body temporarily. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the main difference between resident and transient microbiota?

options.A: Transient flora multiply rapidly inside internal organs unlike resident flora
options.B: Resident flora cause severe infections while transient flora are completely harmless
options.C: Resident flora are acquired from soil while transient flora are inherited at birth
options.D: Resident flora stay permanently, while transient flora are temporary visitors

explanation: You've got this! Resident microbes live permanently on the host as part of our normal makeup, whereas transient microbes are just short-term visitors picked up from our surroundings. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which microorganism is most commonly found colonizing the healthy human skin?
explanation: Staphylococcus epidermidis is a primary resident of human skin. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why is Lactobacillus so common in the healthy adult vaginal microbiome?

options.A: It enters the area through contaminated drinking water
options.B: It thrives in the acidic environment created by glycogen breakdown
options.C: It requires high levels of oxygen found in the reproductive tract
options.D: It feeds directly on circulating red blood cells

explanation: Lactobacillus species produce helpful lactic acid, keeping the area at a low pH which naturally protects you against harmful pathogens. Great nursing knowledge to keep in mind! [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h3)

question: When does the initial acquisition of normal flora primarily begin in humans?

options.D: During the second trimester of pregnancy

explanation: Contact with the birth canal and outside environment during birth initiates microbial colonization. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h4)

question: How does the way a baby is delivered affect their early microbiome?

options.A: Vaginal birth prevents any bacterial contact until solid food is introduced
options.B: Cesarean delivery guarantees total sterility of the infant gut for one year
options.C: Vaginal birth exposes the baby to maternal birth canal flora like Lactobacillus
options.D: Cesarean delivery passes down specialized skin flora directly from the placenta

explanation: Think of the birth canal as the baby's very first introduction to helpful microbes! Passing through it transfers essential maternal flora to the newborn. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which vitamin is synthesized by normal flora in the human gut?
explanation: Gut bacteria play a major role in producing vitamin K, which is necessary for blood clotting. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h5)

question: What do we mean by 'microbial antagonism' provided by normal flora?

options.A: Preventing pathogen growth by competing for space and nutrients
options.B: Directly attacking host immune cells to suppress inflammation
options.C: Releasing toxins that destroy beneficial human cells in the gut
options.D: Absorbing all available oxygen in the bloodstream

explanation: It's like turf war in the body! Resident microbes take up all the space and food, leaving no room for nasty pathogens to settle down. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h5)

question: What type of pathogen causes disease only when the host immune system is weakened?
explanation: Opportunistic organisms wait for a vulnerability in host defenses to cause an infection. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why can taking broad-spectrum antibiotics sometimes lead to a secondary yeast infection?

options.A: Antibiotics stimulate the rapid reproduction of fungal cell walls
options.B: Antibiotics destroy protective normal flora that usually keep yeast growth in check
options.C: Antibiotics lower body temperature enough to encourage fungal spore germination
options.D: Antibiotics mutate harmless skin fungi into aggressive toxin-producing strains

explanation: Antibiotics kill bacteria indiscriminately. When the good protective bacteria are wiped out, fungi like Candida get a chance to overgrow without competition! [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the single most effective nursing action to prevent spreading transient microbes?
explanation: Simple and classic! Thorough handwashing is your number one tool as a nurse to remove transient microorganisms picked up from patients or the hospital environment. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h7)

question: Why must you use strict aseptic technique when inserting a urinary catheter?

options.A: To accelerate the natural production of protective resident flora
options.B: To keep the external genitalia completely free of all bacteria
options.C: To ensure the patient does not experience allergic reactions to latex
options.D: To prevent introducing skin flora into the normally sterile bladder

explanation: You're protecting the patient! Aseptic technique stops outside microbes from riding along the catheter and entering the sterile bladder, preventing a UTI. [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h7)
